Subject: Plan rules: surge upgrades + feature tethering for our pilot

Hi Sergio —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We shared the transcript with our ops and product teams; a couple of follow-ups from them:

1) Surge eligibility: if our pilot exceeds the committed throughput during a 2‑week marketing push, what is the upgrade path mid-contract? Do you require an amendment vs. an automatic temporary burst credit?

2) Feature tethering: our security/compliance team wants to know whether certain features (notably private VPC and audit log retention) are tied to a specific plan tier and therefore unavailable during an in-flight upgrade/downgrade. Can you confirm which features are "tethered"?

Attached: Atlas_MVP_Rollout_Reqs.pdf (high-level traffic forecast + must-have features).

Can we get a short written summary we can attach to our procurement packet (they prefer a one-page entry outlining upgrade mechanics and feature availability)?

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Plan rules: surge upgrades + feature tethering for our pilot

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Quick summary for your procurement team below (I kept this intentionally short so it can sit in your packet):

- Surge upgrades: we support two mechanisms.
  * Temporary burst credits: automatic, non‑contractual, intended for short spikes (<48 hours). No contract amendment required; billed at list per‑token rates after credits.
  * Mid‑contract upgrade: for sustained higher throughput (2+ weeks), we recommend a formal tier upgrade (amendment). This gives predictable unit economics and access to dedicated capacity options.

- Policy triggers: if sustained usage > 120% of committed throughput for 7 consecutive days our system will notify both teams and suggest the upgrade pathway. We never auto‑upgrade without customer agreement.

- Feature tethering: features in Redwood are either "portable" or "tethered":
  * Portable (available across tiers): basic generation, embeddings, standard observability, streaming.
  * Tethered (requires explicit tier or Dedicated/Private add-on): private VPC, extended audit retention (beyond 90 days), HSM/KMS-managed keys, SLA-backed dedicated pools.

Notes specific to Atlas from the attachment: given your projected 3x peak during the push, we recommend either:
  1) Keep current tier + pre‑purchase burst credits for the two weeks (lower up‑front cost, easy rollback), or
  2) Execute a 60‑day pilot amendment to move to the "Throughput Plus" tier (adds private VPC & extended logs, and reduces per‑token cost by ~18%).

Next steps I suggest:
- Kimberly, can you confirm the tech constraints for switching extended audit retention mid‑pilot? If there are data‑migration hiccups we should note them for procurement.
- Maya, if you want the one‑pager I can convert this into a PDF and include the billing example.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20min call later today if that helps.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jun 22, 2026 at 11:45 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hey team — quick technical clarifications from my side (I reviewed the attachment):
>
> - Extended audit retention ("extended_logs") is implemented as a separate storage tier. Moving an account to extended retention is a config toggle but requires a short background job to reindex metadata; typically a 2–6 hour maintenance window to ensure search/query integrity. No customer data leaves your VPC when on Private; if you move from Hosted->Private we do a one‑time migration plan.
>
> - Private VPC is a deployment mode, not a plan feature per se. For pilots we can do a temporary private network for 30 days; beyond that we require Dedicated or Private licensing.
>
> - If Atlas needs HSM-backed keys mid‑pilot, that is considered an add‑on (procurement amendment). Implementation lead time ~10 business days.
>
> I can draft a one‑page tech note (short bullets + expected timelines) that matches Sergio's procurement summary.
>
> -Kim
